title: Like a Weaned Child
superscription: A song of ascents. Of David.

verses.text: My heart is not proud, O LORD, my eyes are not haughty. I do not aspire to great things or matters too lofty for me.
Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul; like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
O Israel, put your hope in the LORD, both now and forevermore.

context.author: The title says “A song of ascents. Of David.” They may have been sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts; the Mishnah says the Levites sang them on the fifteen steps inside the Temple courts (Sukkah 5:4).
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: Three verses of quiet humility. “My heart is not proud, O LORD, my eyes are not haughty. I do not aspire to great things or matters too lofty for me” (v.1). Instead: “Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul; like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me” (v.2). Then the lesson for all: “O Israel, put your hope in the LORD, both now and forevermore” (v.3).
context.custom: Children were often weaned at two or three years old, and weaning was celebrated (Genesis 21:8; 1 Samuel 1:22-24). A nursing baby frets for milk, but a weaned child sits contentedly with its mother, wanting her presence, not only what she gives.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 132 remembers David’s oath to find a home for the ark.
context.timelineBible: Jesus said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 18:3). Paul wrote, “I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances” (Philippians 4:11). Peter says, “Humble yourselves, therefore, under God’s mighty hand” (1 Peter 5:6).

otBackground.note: In quiet confidence is your strength.

overview.summary: David has given up pride and great ambitions and quieted his soul like a weaned child resting with its mother, and calls Israel to hope in the LORD.
overview.settingLine: A child at rest with its mother.

history.t: He waited years for the throne.

archaeology.t: Clay figurines of women holding children from Iron Age Judah.
Small spouted clay vessels thought to be used for feeding infants.

overview.discussion: A weaned child wants its mother, not just her milk (v.2). Do I seek God for Himself, or mainly for what He gives?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
overview.genre: Song of ascents; psalm of trust
